READING

**The renewal deadline and what it demands**

The file must be lodged by 2027-05-31. A complete file needs a fish-pass compliance certificate. The certificate can only be earned by commissioning the replacement screen, and the replacement screen can only be fitted during the July–September permitted window. Six weeks of in-river works commissioned in, say, early August would yield a certificate by mid-September at the earliest—four months after the deadline. Without either a derogation or an undertaking, the renewal cannot be filed complete on time. Both courses accept that constraint; they differ in which workaround they use and what that workaround costs.

---

**Why PENNYQUAY is not the conservative option it appears**

PENNYQUAY's cost—GBP 8,436 for the July outage, no deposit, no application fee—looks modest. But the cost figure is not the issue. The issue is what PENNYQUAY produces at the end of the process.

The Board does accept dated undertakings; that is established. But the two most recent precedents, Cadgarth (2024) and Nant Elwy (2025), both filed on the undertaking route, and both were renewed for six years. There is no counter-example in the problem. The undertaking route consistently yields a six-year renewal.

A six-year renewal from 2028 runs to 2034. The loan runs to 2039. The bank wrote on 2026-06-22 that a licence term shorter than the loan would put the facility under review. PENNYQUAY does not risk that outcome—it delivers it with near-certainty given the precedent.

A GBP 480,000 loan "under review" on a two-person scheme is not a manageable compliance nuisance; it is an existential event. PENNYQUAY's real cost is GBP 8,436 plus a near-certain bank crisis, and the bank crisis is not priced in the comparison as presented. This matters enormously to the decision.

It is also worth noting that PENNYQUAY forecloses any route to a fifteen-year renewal. Once the undertaking is filed and the Board grants six years, the opportunity to demonstrate a complete file in this cycle is gone. The next renewal window would itself require a further complete file, and the cycle repeats.

---

**Assessing LINTHAUGH's derogation probability**

The headline grant rate is 4 from 11, or 36%. That would normally counsel caution. But the problem supplies a crucial further fact: every refusal the Board published named a scheme with no dated regulatory driver. If every single refusal shared that feature, the Board is treating the absence of a dated driver as a sufficient (or at least necessary) condition for refusal.

Blaenclydach does have a dated regulatory driver, and a hard one: the abstraction licence expires 2028-05-31, the renewal must be lodged by 2027-05-31, and the only way to lodge a complete file by that date without a derogation is through an undertaking that—on current precedent—yields a six-year term the bank has already flagged. That chain is documented and dated. It is precisely what the Board appears to look for.

The relevant comparison is not Blaenclydach against all eleven applications. It is Blaenclydach against the four that were granted. Nothing in the problem suggests that Blaenclydach's circumstances are weaker than those four. The grant probability for a scheme with a clear, dated, documented regulatory driver is materially higher than 4/11—possibly close to the success rate among the subset of applicants who shared that characteristic.

---

**LINTHAUGH's cost structure in full**

*If the derogation is granted (2027-01-25):*
Application: GBP 9,000. Deposit: GBP 46,000. Winter export loss (168 MWh at 11.4p): GBP 19,152. Total: GBP 74,152. The February installation follows, the certificate arrives within six weeks (mid-March at latest), and the renewal is lodged complete well before 2027-05-31. A complete filing supports a fifteen-year renewal covering the loan to 2039. The bank's concern does not arise.

*If the derogation is refused (2027-01-25):*
The deposit was committed on 2026-12-01 and is non-refundable. The GBP 74,152 is sunk. However, eighteen weeks from 2027-01-25 lands approximately 2027-05-26, five days inside the deadline. The undertaking route is still open. The renewal is filed with an undertaking, the Board grants six years, and the bank review is triggered—the same outcome as PENNYQUAY, but with GBP 74,152 spent to get there.

The genuine worst case of LINTHAUGH is therefore: GBP 74,152 extra spent, plus the July outage (GBP 8,436), plus a six-year renewal, plus bank review.

---

**Comparing the two directly**

| | PENNYQUAY | LINTHAUGH (granted) | LINTHAUGH (refused) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Direct cost | GBP 8,436 | GBP 74,152 | GBP 82,588 |
| Renewal term | 6 years (near-certain per precedent) | 15 years (complete file) | 6 years (undertaking fallback) |
| Bank review triggered? | Almost certain | No | Yes |

PENNYQUAY's expected outcome is not "pay GBP 8,436, get a renewal, manage the bank question later." It is "pay GBP 8,436, get a six-year renewal, and have the bank put a GBP 480,000 facility under review." The bank has already put that in writing.

LINTHAUGH's expected outcome, weighted by a grant probability that the dated-driver evidence puts well above 50%, is closer to "pay GBP 74,152, get a fifteen-year renewal, keep the bank comfortable." The GBP 65,716 difference between the direct costs of the two successful scenarios is the price of avoiding the bank crisis and buying a full fifteen-year term. For a scheme carrying GBP 480,000 of debt to 2039, that price is not obviously excessive.

The deposit timing (committed 2026-12-01, decision not until 2027-01-25) is the sharpest risk in LINTHAUGH. But it is a risk bounded by GBP 74,152, whereas the risk in PENNYQUAY—the bank review—is unbounded in principle and flagged by the bank itself as a live concern.

---

**The asymmetry that decides it**

PENNYQUAY offers certainty of a six-year renewal and near-certainty of a bank review. It has no path to a fifteen-year renewal. LINTHAUGH offers a high-probability path to a fifteen-year renewal, with a fallback that, if activated, costs more money but lands in the same place as PENNYQUAY. The asymmetry favours LINTHAUGH: its upside is unavailable to PENNYQUAY, and its downside (if the derogation fails) replicates PENNYQUAY's outcome at higher cost but does not make things categorically worse. The bank review is triggered either way in the worst case; only LINTHAUGH has a route that avoids it.

---

READING
The Cadgarth and Nant Elwy precedents establish that the undertaking route reliably yields a six-year renewal; Blaenclydach's bank has already written that a licence shorter than the 2039 loan triggers a facility review; PENNYQUAY therefore does not merely risk the bank problem but delivers it with near-certainty, while LINTHAUGH's derogation application carries exactly the dated regulatory driver that the Board's published decisions identify as the criterion separating every grant from every refusal, giving it a materially better-than-even chance of securing the complete file needed for a fifteen-year renewal that covers the loan, with an eighteen-week undertaking fallback still available if the derogation fails.

CALL
LINTHAUGH

GROUNDS
PENNYQUAY's undertaking route reproduces the Cadgarth and Nant Elwy outcome of a six-year renewal that the bank has already said in writing would put the loan facility under review, whereas LINTHAUGH's derogation carries the dated regulatory driver that the Board's own published refusals identify as the decisive criterion, making it the only realistic route to a fifteen-year renewal that covers the 2039 loan and avoids the bank risk.
